Last winter a slight accident took place, and there was consternation all over the island when it was reported that one of the propellers of the boat had been broken off and that she would have to go to Halifax for repairs in the middle of the winter. An embargo was placed on all freight at a time when it was very important and desirable to move it, especially potatoes, and it is indeed iucky that in the fourteen or fifteen years that boat has been operating a more serious accident has not occurred,
The minister's explanation in regard to the whole matter has been very clear and explicit. With respect to the proposals for a tunnel or causeway, I am of the opinion, as the minister is, that under the existing conditions a car ferry service is as much as we can ask for, especially in view of the enormous amount of money which either a tunnel or a causeway would involve. It is very gratifying that all arrangements have been undertaken to provide particularly for automobile traffic, because, as the minister said, when the present boat was built there was a prohibition against automobiles on the island, and such a thing as carrying automobiles was not contemplated. My only reason for speaking at all of the present con-
Supply-Railways-Car Ferry

dition is to urge that all possible haste be made in the carrying out of the proposals, and that the boat be provided and put into service at the earliest possible date.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I move that vote No. 93 be reduced by $1,000,000.
Motion agreed to.
Will the minister tell me where the tenders are being called? Are they public tenders-I mean both Canadian and British? Where will the boat be built, in Canada or in Britain?
We have scarcely reached that point yet, but if there is a Canadian firm that has the facilities I should like to give it an opportunity.

Surely there must be
some.

It is a very special type of construction. The existing boat was built in the old country, at Newcastle on Tyne, I believe. Certainly there will be public tenders, or at least tenders addressed' to any concerns which might reasonably be expected to be able to supply the type desired.
Is it the intention when this boat is built to have the two kept on the service?
Yes.
What revenue has been derived from the ferry as it has been running?

It cannot be segregated inasmuch as it is a part of the railway service. I can give information regarding trips of the ferry, if that will help. The trips per month in 1928 reached a higher average than for many years; I believe it was the highest average in the history of the ferry. There were 160 round trips per month in 1928. The number of passengers per annum is also increasing; in 1928 it was 73,000. The automobiles are increasing; the number reached the total, higher than ever before, of 7,416 in 1928.
It is recommended in the Duncan report that a separate accounting be made of the ferry service, as distinct from the accounting for the Island railways. Has the minister considered that?

I do not remember a recommendation with respect to a separate accounting for the Island railways, but I do remember something of that sort in connection with the operation of the ferry. I suggest, however, that it would be very cum-
bersome and difficult. We are really meeting the intention by providing this ferry, not to be charged to the Canadian National Railways, but to the funds of the Dominion of Canada directly.
But not the operation.

No; its operation forms a part of the operation of the eastern lines and meets the intention of the Duncan report rather better than an elaborate accounting which would have very wide ramifications. For instance, I mentioned 73,000 passengers: a separate accounting would involve the separation of that portion of each passenger's fare which could be properly allocated to the ferry. And the same with freight, which is a through movement. Separate accounting would be unnecessarily cumbersome and would not be of advantage, whereas this method involves the assumption by the Dominion of the constitutional responsibility which belongs to the Dominion in providing the capital expenditure involved.

Has the minister any idea
whether the boat when completed will pay capital charge and operating expenses?

The annual cost of operation, including interest and depreciation on the scheme we are now proposing, would be $804,800. I cannot give accurate figures with regard to the revenue 'but am reasonably sure we cannot hope that the revenue would meet the cost of providing the service which is the carrying out of an obligation of confederation.
What is the fare across?

There is no separate
fare; it is included in the railway fare.
It is a free service?
No.

I understand that the fare for a single crossing is 75 cents and the charge for automobiles $4. The point raised by my hon. friend (Mr. MacLaren) is of considerable importance. The cost of operation certainly cannot be taken care of by passenger traffic, and under present methods of operating it increases the deficit on the railway line there. That, in turn, is charged to the eastern lines, and when railway matters are discussed the charge is always made-and it is a fact-that there is a loss on these lines. The loss would be minimized to a considerable extent if this ferry, which is a direct obligation of the Dominion and is not part of the railway service, could be taken out of the Railway department altogether in the matter of expenditures. In regard to

the work done last year, I gathered from the statement made that about $220,000 was expended out of the $1,000,000 voted. Can the minister give us an idea as to what was done?
That does not appear to be on my file. If I can supply the information privately to my hon. friend I shall be glad to let him have the details.

One hon. member told
me that he wanted certain details and I should be glad if the minister would report progress. It is eleven o'clock anyhow.

Is any part of the depreciation and fixed charges upon the investment which the minister mentioned a moment ago taken into consideration in determining the deficit in the operation of the eastern line?

No.
Progress reported.
